content.content:
- **Privilege:** **Read Computers**. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v4-computers-inventory.md
  - `/api/v3/computers-inventory` is `deprecated: true`, `x-deprecation-date: 2026-07-14` (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-computers-inventory.md). [PD], dated May 2026, still shows v3 as N/A.
  - Earlier versions: v1 deprecated 2025-06-30, v2 deprecated 2025-11-06 [PD].
  - Classic `/JSSResource/computers` was deprecated on 2025-02-11 [CP].
- **Parameters:**
  - `section` (repeatable; default `GENERAL`). Values: `GENERAL`, `DISK_ENCRYPTION`, `PURCHASING`, `APPLICATIONS`, `STORAGE`, `USER_AND_LOCATION`, `CONFIGURATION_PROFILES`, `PRINTERS`, `SERVICES`, `HARDWARE`, `LOCAL_USER_ACCOUNTS`, `CERTIFICATES`, `ATTACHMENTS`, `PACKAGE_RECEIPTS`, `SECURITY`, `OPERATING_SYSTEM`, `LICENSED_SOFTWARE`, `IBEACONS`, `SOFTWARE_UPDATES`, `EXTENSION_ATTRIBUTES`, `CONTENT_CACHING`, `GROUP_MEMBERSHIPS`
  - `page`, `page-size` (default 100; no maximum declared, so UNVERIFIED)
  - `sort` (default `general.name:asc`)
  - `filter` (RSQL)
- **Filterable fields of interest** (from the filter description):
  - `general.lastContact`, `general.lastCheckIn`, `general.reportDate`, `general.remoteManagement.managed`, `general.mdmCapable.capable`, `general.supervised`, `general.userApprovedMdm`, `general.enrolledViaAutomatedDeviceEnrollment`, `general.declarativeDeviceManagementEnabled`, `general.mdmCertificateExpiration`
  - `operatingSystem.version`, `operatingSystem.fileVault2Status`
  - `diskEncryption.fileVault2Enabled`
  - `security.firewallEnabled`, `security.activationLockEnabled`, `security.recoveryLockEnabled`, `security.lockdownModeEnabled`
  - Notes:
    - There is no `lastContactTime`; the field is `general.lastContact`.
    - The filter and sort lists name `general.mdmCertificateExpiration`, but the `ComputerGeneralV4` schema field is `mdmProfileExpiration`.
    - SIP and Gatekeeper status cannot be filtered; read them from the response.
- **`ComputerGeneralV4` fields:**
  - date-times: `lastContact`, `lastCheckIn`, `reportDate`, `lastEnrolledDate`, `mdmProfileExpiration`
  - `remoteManagement{managed, managementUsername}`
  - `mdmCapable{capable, capableUsers, userManagementInfo}`
  - booleans: `supervised`, `userApprovedMdm`, `enrolledViaAutomatedDeviceEnrollment`, `declarativeDeviceManagementEnabled`
  - `platform`, `site`
- **`ComputerOperatingSystem` fields:** `name`, `version`, `build`, `supplementalBuildVersion`, `rapidSecurityResponse`, `fileVault2Status` (enum `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `NOT_ENCRYPTED`, `BOOT_ENCRYPTED`, `SOME_ENCRYPTED`, `ALL_ENCRYPTED`)
- **`ComputerDiskEncryption` fields:**
  - `individualRecoveryKeyValidityStatus`: enum `VALID`, `INVALID`, `UNKNOWN`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`
  - `institutionalRecoveryKeyPresent`: boolean
  - `diskEncryptionConfigurationName`, `fileVault2EligibilityMessage`: string
  - `fileVault2Enabled`: boolean
  - `fileVault2EnabledUserNames`: [string]
  - `bootPartitionEncryptionDetails{partitionName, partitionFileVault2State, partitionFileVault2Percent}`
  - The `partitionFileVault2State` enum is `UNKNOWN`, `UNENCRYPTED`, `INELIGIBLE`, `DECRYPTED`, `DECRYPTING`, `ENCRYPTED`, `ENCRYPTING`, `RESTART_NEEDED`, `OPTIMIZING`, `DECRYPTING_PAUSED`, `ENCRYPTING_PAUSED`.
- **`ComputerSecurity` fields:**
  - `sipStatus`: enum `NOT_COLLECTED`, `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `DISABLED`, `ENABLED`
  - `gatekeeperStatus`: enum `NOT_COLLECTED`, `DISABLED`, `APP_STORE_AND_IDENTIFIED_DEVELOPERS`, `APP_STORE`
  - booleans: `firewallEnabled`, `autoLoginDisabled`, `remoteDesktopEnabled`, `activationLockEnabled`, `recoveryLockEnabled`, `bootstrapTokenAllowed`, `lockdownModeEnabled`
  - `secureBootLevel`: enum `NO_SECURITY`, `MEDIUM_SECURITY`, `FULL_SECURITY`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`, `UNKNOWN`
  - `externalBootLevel`: enum `ALLOW_BOOTING_FROM_EXTERNAL_MEDIA`, `DISALLOW_BOOTING_FROM_EXTERNAL_MEDIA`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`, `UNKNOWN`
  - `bootstrapTokenEscrowedStatus`: enum `ESCROWED`, `NOT_ESCROWED`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`
  - `attestationStatus`: enum, plus `lastAttestationAttempt` and `lastSuccessfulAttestation`
  - `xprotectVersion`: string
- **Do not use** (secret-revealing endpoints):
  - `GET /api/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/filevault` and `/v4/computers-inventory/filevault` need **View Disk Encryption Recovery Key** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v4-computers-inventory-id-filevault.md).
  - `/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/view-recovery-lock-password` needs **View Recovery Lock** ([PD] for v1–v3).
  - `/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/view-device-lock-pin` also exists in the index.
- **Example request:**
  `GET /api/v4/computers-inventory?section=GENERAL&section=OPERATING_SYSTEM&section=DISK_ENCRYPTION&section=SECURITY&page=0&page-size=100&filter=general.remoteManagement.managed==true`
- **Sample response (illustrative):**
  `{"totalCount":2,"results":[{"id":"1","general":{"name":"Mac-01","lastContact":"2026-11-08T10:00:00Z","remoteManagement":{"managed":true}},"operatingSystem":{"version":"26.1","fileVault2Status":"ALL_ENCRYPTED"},"diskEncryption":{"individualRecoveryKeyValidityStatus":"VALID"},"security":{"sipStatus":"ENABLED","gatekeeperStatus":"APP_STORE_AND_IDENTIFIED_DEVELOPERS","firewallEnabled":true}}]}`

## 11. Mobile device inventory

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v2/mobile-devices/detail`
- **Privilege:** **Read Mobile Devices**; not deprecated (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v2-mobile-devices-detail.md; [PD])
- **Sections:** `GENERAL`, `HARDWARE`, `USER_AND_LOCATION`, `PURCHASING`, `SECURITY`, `APPLICATIONS`, `EBOOKS`, `NETWORK`, `SERVICE_SUBSCRIPTIONS`, `CERTIFICATES`, `PROFILES`, `USER_PROFILES`, `PROVISIONING_PROFILES`, `SHARED_USERS`, `GROUPS`, `EXTENSION_ATTRIBUTES`. There is no OPERATING_SYSTEM section; the OS fields are in GENERAL.
- **`exception-handling`:** `STRICT` (default) returns a 500 for a device with data problems. `LENIENT` returns 200 with that section null. A pack should use `LENIENT`.
- **Default sort:** `displayName:asc`
- **Filter fields include:** `managed`, `supervised`, `osVersion`, `lastInventoryUpdateDate`, `lastContactDate`, `passcodeCompliant`, `passcodeCompliantWithProfile`, `passcodePresent`, `dataProtection`, `activationLockEnabled`, `lockdownModeEnabled`, `lostModeEnabled`, `awaitingConfiguration`, `groupId`, `groupName`
- **GENERAL fields:**
  - `osVersion`, `osBuild`, `osRapidSecurityResponse`, `lastInventoryUpdateDate`, `lastContactDate`, `lastEnrolledDate`, `mdmProfileExpirationDate`
  - booleans: `managed`, `supervised`, `enrollmentSessionTokenValid`
  - `deviceOwnershipType`: enum `Institutional`, `UserEnrollment`, `AccountDrivenUserEnrollment`, `AccountDrivenDeviceEnrollment`
  - `appleEnrollmentType`: enum `none`, `supervised`, `device`, `user`, `unknown`
- **SECURITY fields:**
  - booleans: `dataProtected`, `passcodePresent`, `passcodeCompliant`, `passcodeCompliantWithProfile`, `jailBreakDetected`, `activationLockEnabled`, `lostModeEnabled`, `lockdownModeEnabled`
  - `hardwareEncryption`: integer
  - `attestationStatus`: enum
  - `bootstrapTokenEscrowed`: enum string `ESCROWED`, `NOT_ESCROWED`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`
- **Naming mismatches:**
  - The filter field `dataProtection` corresponds to the schema field `dataProtected`.
  - `jailbreakStatus` appears only in the sort list. It is not filterable, so read `security.jailBreakDetected` from the response.

## 12. Audit and change management

- **Change Management:** no API was found for its settings or logs in the JPAPI or Classic index.
  - "The option to log changes to a log file or a syslog server is only available for on-premise environments." The file is `JAMFChangeManagement.log`. On Jamf Cloud, changes "are automatically displayed in the Change Management settings and cannot be exported". Source: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Change_Management
  - Jamf Log Stream is "available only to customers of the Jamf Cloud Premium offering". It sends Change Management and Access logs to Splunk, Amazon S3, Datadog or an HTTPS endpoint. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-log-stream.md
  - An API to check whether Log Stream is configured is UNVERIFIED and none was found.
  - STIG V-241793 (medium) requires logs to be transferred to another server.
- **Log flushing (retention):** `GET /api/v1/log-flushing` returns `{retentionPolicies: [{displayName, qualifier, retentionPeriod: integer, retentionPeriodUnit: string}], hourOfDay: integer}`.
- Whether `/v1/notifications` returns data to an API client.
- That `ssoBypassAllowed` maps to the UI's "Allow users to bypass" option.
- The HTTP status Jamf Cloud returns when it rejects requests under load.
- Whether a Classic webhook GET returns `password` in clear text.
- That "All LDAP Users" cannot be deleted.
- The subset syntax for the Classic profile endpoint.
- The 11.33.x release dates, which come from secondary sources.

## Corrections

1. **Cluster refresh.** The sticky-sessions guide says "up to a 60 second delay" and does not say the cluster "refreshes every minute". It also says the cookie name "may vary based on hosting region".
2. **Rate limiting on Jamf Cloud.** `/v1/health-status` describes ratios of accepted to denied requests, so Jamf Cloud does reject requests under load. The page documents 200 and 404 only. It requires authentication (`x-authentication-required: true`) but no privilege; the earlier report did not state this.
3. **Mobile filter fields.** `jailbreakStatus` is a sort field only, not a filter field. Filtering on jailbreak status is impossible; read `security.jailBreakDetected` from the response.
4. **Mobile `bootstrapTokenEscrowed`** is an enum string (`ESCROWED`/`NOT_ESCROWED`/`NOT_SUPPORTED`), not a boolean. The SECURITY section also holds `lostModeEnabled`.
5. **v4 SECURITY enums.** The full `secureBootLevel` enum is `NO_SECURITY`, `MEDIUM_SECURITY`, `FULL_SECURITY`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`, `UNKNOWN`. The `externalBootLevel` values are now listed. `lockdownModeEnabled` and the attestation fields were added. The full `partitionFileVault2State` and `section` enums were added.
6. **Inventory filter claims.** SIP and Gatekeeper status cannot be filtered. `general.lastCheckIn`, `general.mdmCapable.capable` and `general.declarativeDeviceManagementEnabled` are filterable.
7. **[PD] is stale for inventory.** [PD] (updated 2026-05-07) does not list `/v4/computers-inventory` and still shows v3 as not deprecated. The v3 deprecation date of 2026-07-14 comes from the v3 reference page, not [PD]. The v4 privilege comes from the v4 reference page.
8. **Default sorts.** Account groups sort by `name:asc` by default, and enrollment access groups by `name:asc`. `/v3/enrollment/access-groups` also takes an `all-users-option-first` parameter.
9. **Access management.** `/v4/enrollment/access-management` returns only `automatedDeviceEnrollmentServerUuid`, so it was marked optional in the role.
10. **v4 enrollment fields.** The `flushMdmCommandsOnReenroll` enum values and defaults were added. Added the fields `flushLocationInformation`, `flushLocationHistoryInformation`, `flushExtensionAttributes`, `flushSoftwareUpdatePlans` and `maidUsernameMergeEnabled`. The certificate and keystore fields are flagged as never to log. `personalDeviceEnrollmentType` was deprecated in 11.25 and always returns "USERENROLLMENT".
11. **SAML fields.** Added `userAttributeName`, `groupRdnKey`, `metadataFileName`, `otherProviderTypeName` and `federationMetadataFile`. `groupAttributeName` defaults to the ADFS group claim URI, and `usernameAttributeClaimMapping` is an enum `USERNAME`/`EMAIL`.
12. **Log flushing.** `retentionPeriodUnit` is a plain string with example values, not a declared enum.
13. **Classic profile fields.** `redeploy_on_update` is a string, for example "Newly Assigned". `general` also has `description`, `site` and `category`. The Classic spec version is 11.32.0.
14. **Classic webhooks.** The schema includes `password`, `enable_display_fields_for_group_object` and `display_fields`. `content_type` is `text/xml`|`application/json`. The pack should drop `password`.
15. **Mobile profile privilege.** The API role string is probably "Read iOS Configuration Profiles" (third-party), not "Mobile Device Configuration Profiles".
16. **Never-grant list.** Added the v4 secret endpoints: `/v4/computers-inventory/filevault`, `/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/view-recovery-lock-password` and `/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/view-device-lock-pin`. Also added "View Local Admin Password Audit History" and "Dismiss Notifications".
17. **New endpoint for STIG V-241794.** `GET /api/v1/login-customization` needs no privilege and reports `includeCustomDisclaimer` and the banner text.
18. **STIG gaps.** Added V-241791 (15-minute session lock), V-241794 (banner) and V-241817 (disable installation-time local accounts). V-241798 also has rule SV-241798r971326_rule and version JAMF-10-000700, and its stale version list appears in both the check text and the fix text.
19. **Basic auth before 11.17.** Between 11.5.0 and 11.17.0, an option in the UI could relax the token-only restriction.
20. **Missing privilege statements.** `/v1/notifications`, `/v1/health-status` and `/v2/jamf-pro-information` require authentication but no named privilege. "No privilege" does not mean no authentication.
21. **`/v2/jamf-pro-information`.** The endpoint is not deprecated; only its `byodEnabled` field is (11.25).
22. **Log Stream.** It covers Change Management and Access logs and is available only on Jamf Cloud Premium.

content.content:
288 website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md
---
title: Attribute rubric
description: How to choose the classification, priority and mapping attributes of a Maester test, and how those choices are checked.
sidebar:
  order: 2
---

# Attribute rubric

Every test shipped with Maester declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
it addresses. This page is the rule book for those values. Unit tests check what can be checked mechanically, and
a review step checks the judgement calls against this page. A custom test may use the same attributes; the rules
apply to it only if you want them to.

The [test builder](/test-builder) lets you pick the values with this guidance beside each field and
shows the code as you go.

| Question | Attributes | Required for built-in tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` | All except `RelatedProduct` |
| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` | `Severity` always. The other two unless `Severity` is `Info` |
| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` | `Mitre` (technique IDs or `None`) |
| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` | No. `Lifecycle` defaults to `Stable` |

The allowed keys for `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are in
[`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1).
Add a key there in the same pull request as the first test that needs it.

## Rate the test, not your tenant

Rate every value for a typical organization that fails the test, using the fix the test's own Markdown file
recommends. Do not rate for the best case, the worst case or one tenant you know. When two values fit, choose the
lower one for `Severity`, `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost`. A reader should be able to see the reason for
each value in the test's description and remediation text.

## Product

The product where the fix is made. One value.

- Use the product whose admin surface holds the setting, not every product the test reads from.
- Tests in a product folder (`tests/maester/entra`, `tests/cisa/exchange`) use that folder's product.
- A product the test only reads from, or a licence it needs, is not a second product. `Service` and `License`
  already say that.

## RelatedProduct

Other products the test also checks or depends on. Optional list, never the same key as `Product`.

- Add one when an admin of that product would expect to find the test under it. An Exchange Online test about an
  anti-phishing policy that is managed in the Defender portal has `RelatedProduct = 'defender'`.
- Add one when the fix is made in that product's portal although the test lives in another product's folder.
- Do not add a product only because its API is called.

## Feature

The part of the product the test is about. One key from the product's `Features` list.

- Choose the feature whose settings page or object type the remediation sends the admin to.
- When a test spans two features, choose the one that fails most directly. A Conditional Access policy that
  requires a compliant device is `conditional-access`, not `devices`.
- Tests that check the same thing get the same feature, whatever folder or suite they are in.
- A feature that would hold one test only is usually too narrow. Prefer an existing feature.

## Area

The security theme, whatever the product. One key.

| Key | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `authentication` | How an identity proves who it is: MFA, authentication methods, passwords, legacy protocols, Kerberos and NTLM hardening, session and token lifetime. |
| `privileged-access` | Administrative roles and accounts: who holds them, just-in-time elevation, emergency access, admin tiering, delegated admin rights. |
| `access-control` | Who may reach which resource under which conditions: device, location and risk conditions, permissions on objects, user defaults. |
| `applications` | App registrations, service principals and their credentials, consent and API permissions, OAuth apps, add-ins, connectors. |
| `external-access` | Guests, cross-tenant access, federation and trusts, external sharing and external communication. |
| `devices` | Device compliance, enrollment and configuration, endpoint protection, device identity. |
| `email-protection` | Anti-phishing, anti-spam and anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, mail flow rules, meeting and messaging protections. |
| `data-protection` | Data loss prevention, sensitivity labels, encryption, retention, backup. |
| `logging-and-detection` | Audit logs, diagnostic settings, alert policies, sensors and the health of detection tooling. |
| `identity-lifecycle` | Stale and dormant accounts, ownership, access reviews, entitlement management, group membership hygiene. |
| `infrastructure` | The directory and platform itself: domain controllers, DNS, replication, sites, schema, Group Policy health, protocol hardening, subscriptions, tenant-wide platform settings. |
| `engineering-systems` | DevOps organizations, repositories, pipelines, build identities, the software supply chain. |
| `ai` | AI agents and copilots: who can use and share them, how they authenticate, what data and tools they reach. |

When more than one area fits, choose by what the control is for, in this order:

1. It protects administrators or admin rights: `privileged-access`.
2. It decides how sign-in is proven: `authentication`.
3. It is about an application, service principal or agent as the subject: `applications`, or `ai` for agents.
4. It is about people or data outside the organization: `external-access`.
5. Otherwise the area that names the mechanism: `access-control`, `devices`, `email-protection`,
   `data-protection`, `logging-and-detection`, `identity-lifecycle`, `engineering-systems`, `infrastructure`.

A product never decides the area on its own. An Azure DevOps test about who is a Project Collection Administrator
is `privileged-access`, not `engineering-systems`.

Inventory and health tests with no security theme of their own are `infrastructure`. When no area fits, choose
the closest and say so in the pull request, so the list can be reviewed.

## ResourceType

What a failing result points at. One key.

- `Tenant` when the test evaluates one tenant-, organization-, forest- or domain-wide setting. The result is
  about the environment.
- `Tenant` when the test checks that at least one policy of a kind exists, even when it lists the policies that
  satisfy it. A failing result has nothing to list.
- `Tenant` when the test evaluates the single default or global policy of a kind, because there is one of it and
  it applies to everyone.
- Otherwise the kind of object a failing result lists or counts: `User`, `Application`, `Device`,
  `ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `GroupPolicy` and so on. A test that evaluates every policy and lists the ones that
  fail uses the policy type.
- A test that counts objects for review (an inventory test) uses the type it counts. When no key names that kind
  of object and it is a one-off, use `Tenant`.
- A family test, which yields one result per instance, uses the type of the instance.

## Severity

The risk to the organization while the test fails. Not the effort to fix it and not the disruption of fixing it.

| Value | A failing result means |
| --- | --- |
| `Critical` | An attacker with no special position can take over the tenant, the domain or a privileged identity, or a secret is already exposed. Directly exploitable and wide in reach. |
| `High` | A primary control is missing or weakened for many users or for privileged identities, and common techniques such as phishing, password spray or consent phishing are enough to use it. |
| `Medium` | A defence-in-depth control is missing, or the exposure is limited to a few objects or one workload, or using it needs another weakness first. |
| `Low` | Hardening or hygiene with a small security effect on its own. |
| `Info` | The test reports a fact for review and makes no risk judgement. Info tests are left out of scores. |

Decide in this order:

1. **Reach.** Privileged identities or the whole tenant move the value up. A single workload or a few objects
   move it down.
2. **Directness.** Usable from the internet or by any signed-in user moves it up. Needing an earlier compromise
   moves it down. A password taken by phishing, spray or stuffing is not an earlier compromise: those are the
   common techniques `High` already assumes.
3. **Role of the control.** The main control for a threat rates higher than a second layer behind another control.

`Critical` is rare. If the description cannot say in one sentence how an attacker gets from the failing state to
admin rights or exposed secrets, the value is `High` or lower. A benchmark's own wording does not set the value:
a SHALL policy can be `Medium`.

Five cases come up often:

- **A test that passes whenever its data can be read** is `Info`, whatever the data is about. If the fact
  deserves a severity, the test should fail on it.
- **A failure that is only an outage or untidiness**, such as replication health, an expiring token or an unused
  object, is `Low`. It is `Medium` or higher only when the outage switches off a security control, and then it is
  rated as the loss of that control.
- **Alerts and notifications** are a second layer behind the control they watch, so they are `Medium` at most.
- **The same check in two suites** gets the same value in both. Usually the second is a shim that returns the
  first test's result and declares all of its values; see
  [Tests that another suite already has](./index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).
- **The main control against an attack that starts from a stolen password** is `High`. A second layer behind
  that control is `Medium`. Number matching against MFA fatigue is `High`; showing the app name and location in
  the prompt is `Medium`.

Anchors from existing tests:

| Test | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Group Policy object contains a `cpassword` | `Critical` | Any domain user can read and decrypt the stored password. |
| No domain admin account has a service principal name | `Critical` | Any domain user can request a ticket and crack an admin password offline. |
| Legacy authentication is blocked | `High` | Password spray bypasses MFA for every user. |
| Number matching is required for Authenticator push notifications | `High` | MFA fatigue works against any user once a password is phished. |
| Authenticator shows the app name and location | `Medium` | A second layer behind number matching. |
| Users cannot register applications | `Medium` | Needs a signed-in user and a further step to cause harm. |
| MailTips are enabled for end users | `Low` | A small aid against mis-sent mail. |
| Disabled user count should be retrievable | `Info` | Inventory for review. |
| [EIDSCA.AP14 — users may read other users](/docs/tests/EIDSCA.AP14) | `Info` | Disabling `allowedToReadOtherUsers` is not itself a security finding. Review the restriction because it can disrupt collaboration, user lookup and default features. |

Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment) rates many of the same
Microsoft Entra and Intune settings. Where it has a test for the same setting, compare your value with its risk
level and give the reason in the pull request if the two differ.

## UserImpact

How much the recommended fix disrupts end users. Administrators and the owners of applications are not end
users here. Developers are the end users of Azure DevOps and GitHub.

| Value | Applying the fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | End users notice nothing, or only administrators are affected. |
| `Medium` | Some users change how they work or meet a new prompt: a group loses a capability, users register a method once, a legacy client stops working for a subset. |
| `High` | Most users change a daily habit, or a mistake locks people out or stops mail or an app for many. Needs communication and a staged rollout. |

Omit `UserImpact` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## ImplementationCost

How much administrator work the recommended fix takes.

| Value | The fix is |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | One setting or one policy in one portal. Under an hour, with no dependency on another team, a licence purchase or a rollout. |
| `Medium` | Several steps: a policy that needs exclusions and a pilot, clean-up of a handful of objects, coordination with one other team. Hours to a few days. |
| `High` | A project: new licences, infrastructure or process, a migration of users or apps, or clean-up across many objects. Weeks or more. |

Clean-up that one administrator can finish alone in a sitting is `Low`. Clean-up that needs the owner of each
object is `Medium`. Turning on a plan that is billed by use is `Medium`: the click is easy, the budget approval is
not. Count the work of the fix, including exclusions and rollout, but not the time to decide.

Omit `ImplementationCost` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## Mitre

The MITRE ATT&CK techniques that the checked control prevents or detects. A list of technique IDs, or `None`.

- IDs only, in the form `T1110` or `T1110.003`. Tactic names are looked up from the pinned ATT&CK release
  (`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`) and are never typed.
- Use a sub-technique when the control addresses only that sub-technique. When three or more sub-techniques of
  one technique apply, list the technique instead. Do not list a technique together with one of its own
  sub-techniques.
- List a technique only if the test's description explains, or plainly implies, how the control stops or reveals
  it. At most five.
- A test that implements a benchmark which publishes a mapping, such as CISA SCuBA, starts from that mapping and
  then applies these rules. An ID the pinned release has retired is replaced by its successor in that release,
  found by name.
- The description means the comment-based help and the Markdown file together.
- Use `None` for a test with no attacker behaviour behind it, such as replication health or an inventory count.
  An inventory test lists a technique only when the fact it reports is itself the precondition of that technique,
  such as accounts that do not require Kerberos pre-authentication.
- A retired or unknown ID fails the unit tests.

## Control

Requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports, written `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`, for
example `cis-m365:5.1.5.1`, `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` or `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)`. Optional list. Any test can use
it: one shipped with Maester or one of your own.

- `Control` is the only way a test is mapped to a framework. A CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'` and
  a CISA test carries `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` and an ASD test `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`.
  Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its suite's framework. The unit
  tests check this.
- The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result. Put the
  requirement the test is written for first, and any other requirement it supports after it.
- Use the same attribute for a test that exists for its own reasons and also supports a requirement: a Maester
  test that checks the setting a CISA policy asks for, or a CIS test that also supports a NIST control.
- When the key is a framework shipped with Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`, `essential-eight`, `ism`), the requirement must
  exist in that framework's file. If it is new, add it to the file with its facts. The module build and the unit
  tests fail otherwise.
- Do not repeat the `Related` controls of a requirement. The framework file lists them and Maester adds them to
  the result.
- List a requirement only when a passing result is evidence for it. A test that checks one part of a requirement
  may list it; a test that is merely on the same topic may not.

A reference says the test supports the requirement. It never says the organization complies with it.

### NIST SP 800-53

A test may list the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls its setting implements, as `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`.

- Use an ID from the pinned list, [`powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json):
  a base control (`AC-2`) or an enhancement (`IA-2(1)`). The unit tests reject anything else.
- List a control only when a passing result is direct evidence that it is implemented for what the test checks.
- Prefer the enhancement when the test checks exactly what it says: MFA for privileged accounts is `IA-2(1)`.
  Do not list a base control together with one of its own enhancements.
- At most three, best fit first. Never the policy-and-procedures controls (`AC-1`, `IA-1` and so on).
- A test that only reports a count, or checks health, licensing or tidiness, lists none, unless the count is
  itself what a control asks to be tracked: dormant accounts for `AC-2(3)`.
- A test that implements a CISA SCuBA policy does not list NIST controls. CISA publishes that mapping, the
  framework file carries it as `Related`, and the result gets it from there.

## Lifecycle and ReplacedBy

- `Preview`: new and still changing. Not run unless previews are included.
- `Stable`: the default.
- `Deprecated`: kept so history stays readable. Give `ReplacedBy` when another test took its place.

## Tag

`Tag` holds labels the owner of a test folder finds useful. It is not part of Maester's taxonomy.

- Built-in tests do not carry tags for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence, severity or their own ID.
  Each of those has an attribute or is derived.
- A custom test may tag freely.

## How the rubric is enforced

1. **Unit tests** (`powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1`) fail when a built-in test misses a
   required attribute, uses a key that is not in the taxonomy, pairs a feature with the wrong product, lists a
   retired ATT&CK technique, carries a taxonomy tag, names a requirement that a shipped framework file does not
   have, or is a CIS or CISA test without a `Control` for its own framework.
2. **Attribute review** runs on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes. A
   reviewer model reads the test, its Markdown file and this page, and fails the check when a value does not fit
   the rubric, with the value it expected and the reason. It also sees the attributes of the other tests with the
   same product and feature. It fails a test whose area, resource type or severity differs from the same check in
   another suite, and whose user impact or implementation cost differs when both plainly recommend the same fix.
   MITRE techniques and related products are not compared. A maintainer can overrule it.
3. **Reviewers**, human or agent, apply the same page. See `AGENTS.md`.

content.text:
I changed seven files. All nine checks report `IsValid` from `Get-MtTest -Path` with no Errors or Warnings, and the whole `./spec` passes: 123 tests, 0 failed, including the fleet group's tests and `Pack.Tests.ps1`.

**Changes and reasons**

1. **`Test.MP.JAMF.1019.ps1` / `.md`**
   - Removed `nist-800-53-r5:SC-28` from Control. The check counts only Macs that are already encrypted, so a pass is not evidence of SC-28. Control is now just `nist-800-53-r5:SC-12(1)`.
   - Remediation step 2 named a "FileVault Recovery Key Escrow" payload that I could not confirm exists. It now uses the same path as exemplar 1018: **Security & Privacy** > **FileVault**, or **FileVault** in Jamf Pro 11, with the personal recovery key escrowed to Jamf Pro.
2. **`Test.MP.JAMF.1026.ps1` / `.md`**
   - Changed `IA-5` to `IA-5(1)`, password-based authentication. The rubric prefers the enhancement when the check tests exactly that, and `IA-5(1)` is in the pinned NIST list.
3. **`Test.MP.JAMF.1027.ps1`**
   - Changed Severity from High to Medium. A failing tenant usually has one or a few jailbroken devices, and the rubric's reach rule ("a few objects") gives Medium. UserImpact Low and Cost Medium are unchanged.
4. **`Test.MP.JAMF.1028.ps1` / `.md`**
   - Changed the `MinimumMajorVersion` default from 18 to 26, and updated the comment and guide to match. The guide says Apple patches the current iOS and the one before it. The mSCP framework file already lists `cis-apple-macos-27`, so the 27 releases are out, which makes 26 the oldest supported version.
   - The `deviceType` values are now confirmed. The discriminator in `ref/get_v2-mobile-devices-detail.md` maps `iOS`, `tvOS`, `watchOS` and `visionOS`, so the `tv|watch|vision` filter is correct. I wrote these values into the code comment.
   - Replaced the guessed **iOS Version** criterion with "an OS version criterion".
5. **`Test.MP.JAMF.1023.md` and `Test.MP.JAMF.1028.md`**
   - Removed the guessed paths **Computers** > **Software Updates** and **Mobile Devices** > **Software Updates**. The steps now say "Jamf Pro's managed software updates, or a declarative software update configuration".
6. **`spec/Fleet.Tests.ps1`**
   - The fixtures now use the real `deviceType` values `tvOS` and `watchOS` instead of `appleTv` and `watch`, and I added a `visionOS` device to the 1028 pass case.
   - The 1028 pass case uses 26.0 instead of 18.7, and the fail case uses 18.7.2, to match the new default.

**Checked and left as they are**
- **Fields and enums:** every field and enum the checks use is confirmed in `pro-api.md` or the OpenAPI reference pages. That covers the disk encryption, SIP, Gatekeeper and firewall fields on Macs, `general.lastContact` and `operatingSystem.version`, and on mobile devices `general.displayName`, `osVersion`, `lastInventoryUpdateDate` and the SECURITY section booleans.
- **Code:** null handling, `@()` wrapping, single return values and paged reads are correct. Script blocks only go to `Where-Object -FilterScript` or `ForEach-Object -Process`, never `&`.
- **Attributes:** Area, ResourceType, UserImpact, Cost and Mitre IDs fit the rubric on all nine. Severity and Control fit apart from the changes above.
- **No NIST controls on 1020–1022:** this is correct. The mSCP `Related` lists already carry their NIST controls, for example SI-7 and SI-3 for Gatekeeper, and SC-7 for the firewall.
- **Apple links:** the SIP (`secb7ea06b49`), Gatekeeper (`sec5599b66df`) and security releases (`support.apple.com/en-us/100100`) pages match what I know, but I did not fetch them.

**Still uncertain**
- **Exemplar 1018 breaks the rubric.** It repeats `nist-800-53-r5:SC-28`, which is already in the `Related` list of `system_settings_filevault_enforce`. It isn't one of this group's files, so I left it.
- **Menu paths still from memory:** the SIP criterion in Search Inventory, the "Jailbreak Detected" smart group criterion, the "Issue New Recovery Key" policy action, the "Last Check-in" criterion, and **Settings** > **Computer management** > **Check-In**.
- **Area of 1024 (check-in) is a judgement call.** It is `devices`. The rubric sends inventory and health tests to `infrastructure`, but stale managed devices are mainly a device management concern.
- **1019 Severity Medium and 1021 Severity High are defensible but arguable.** 1019 is about keeping data recoverable rather than stopping an attacker, which could argue for Low. 1021 checks the main control against users opening malicious downloads, which supports High, but users can override Gatekeeper per app.
- **Version defaults:** 1023's default of macOS 15 and 1028's default of 26 assume macOS 27 and iOS 27 have shipped. Users will need to raise them over time.
- **Real tenant:** nothing has been run against a live Jamf Pro server, only the recorded answers in the spec.
